info.description: A public and stable API for interacting with axiom services
info.title: Axiom

get.description: Lists annotations in the organization. Filter by `datasets`, or by a time range with both `start` and `end` at most 100 days apart. Without filters, returns all annotations.

parameters.description: Optional: Filter for dataset names.
parameters.name: datasets

parameters.description: Optional: Filter for events after this date. Use RFC3339 time format.
parameters.name: start

parameters.description: Optional: Filter for events before this date. Use RFC3339 time format.
parameters.name: end

400.description: Invalid `start` or `end`, only one of them set, `end` before `start`, or a range longer than 100 days.

post.description: Creates an annotation on one or more existing datasets. If you omit `time`, Axiom uses the time of the request. `time` can't be in the future.

400.description: Invalid annotation, for example an unknown dataset, a `time` in the future, or an `endTime` before `time`.

get.description: Retrieves an annotation by its ID.

400.description: Invalid annotation ID.

put.description: Updates an annotation. Only the fields you include change. Omitted or empty fields keep their current values, so you can't clear a field.

400.description: Invalid annotation ID or the updated annotation is invalid.

delete.description: Deletes an annotation by its ID.

400.description: Invalid annotation ID.

get.description: Lists the datasets you can read, including datasets shared with your organization, sorted by name. Returns all matching datasets in one response without pagination.

parameters.description: Exclude resolved label objects from each dataset response. The labelIds field is still returned.
parameters.name: exclude

parameters.description: Return datasets assigned every specified label ID.
parameters.name: labelIds

post.description: Creates a dataset. The `name` must be unique in your organization, and `retentionDays` can't exceed the retention window of your plan.

parameters.description: Referrer slug
parameters.name: referrer

400.description: Invalid or reserved `name`, invalid `kind`, `retentionDays` longer than your plan allows, unsupported `edgeDeployment`, or dataset limit reached.

409.description: A dataset with this name already exists.

get.description: Retrieves a dataset by its name.

parameters.description: Exclude resolved label objects from the dataset response. The labelIds field is still returned.
parameters.name: exclude

put.description: Updates the `description` and `retentionDays` of a dataset. Both values are replaced, so omitting `description` clears it, and omitting `retentionDays` or setting it to `0` applies your plan's default retention.

delete.description: Deletes a dataset and queues the permanent deletion of its data. For a dataset shared with your organization, removes it from your organization only. Returns the ID of the deletion job.

200.description: Dataset deleted and data deletion job created.

post.description: Queues a job that rebuilds the field schema of a dataset from its stored events, removing fields that no longer occur in any event. Doesn't delete events. You can vacuum each dataset once per hour.

400.description: The dataset is a metrics dataset.

429.description: The dataset was vacuumed less than an hour ago. Retry after the time in `Retry-After`.

Retry-After.description: The GMT date/time at which the current rate limit window resets.

post.description: Queues the deletion of the listed fields from the dataset schema. Deleted values stay in storage but can't be queried, and ingesting a deleted field again recreates it. You can delete fields once every 5 minutes per dataset.

400.description: Empty `fields`, a field that isn't in the schema, a system field or map field, a locked schema, or a metrics dataset.

429.description: Fields were deleted from this dataset less than 5 minutes ago. Retry after the time in `Retry-After`.

Retry-After.description: The GMT date/time at which the current rate limit window resets.

get.description: Lists the fields in the schema of a dataset with their type, unit, description, and hidden setting. Not supported for metrics datasets.

400.description: The dataset is a metrics dataset.

get.description: Retrieves a field in the schema of a dataset by its name. Not supported for metrics datasets.

400.description: The dataset is a metrics dataset.

404.description: The dataset doesn't exist or the field isn't in its schema.

put.description: Updates the `unit`, `description`, and `hidden` settings of a field. All three are replaced, so omitted values are cleared. The `name` and `type` in the body are ignored.

400.description: A metrics dataset or a dataset managed by Axiom.

404.description: The dataset doesn't exist or the field isn't in its schema.

delete.description: Queues the deletion of a field from the dataset schema. Deleted values stay in storage but can't be queried, and ingesting the field again recreates it. You can delete fields once every 5 minutes per dataset.
delete.summary: Delete a field from a dataset

400.description: A system field or map field, a locked schema, or a metrics dataset.

404.description: The dataset doesn't exist or the field isn't in its schema.

429.description: Fields were deleted from this dataset less than 5 minutes ago. Retry after the time in `Retry-After`.

Retry-After.description: The GMT date/time at which the current rate limit window resets.

get.description: Lists the names of the fields configured as map fields in a dataset.

put.description: Replaces the list of map fields in a dataset. Fields you leave out of the list stop being map fields. Not supported for metrics datasets.

200.description: Map field names after the update.

400.description: Empty, invalid, or duplicate field name, or a metrics dataset.

post.description: Configures a field as a map field. Events you ingest afterward store the field's nested keys inside the map, while previously ingested events keep their structure. Not supported for metrics datasets.

400.description: Empty or invalid field name, or a metrics dataset.

409.description: The field is already a map field.

delete.description: Removes a field from the map fields of a dataset. The field itself and its ingested data aren't deleted. Not supported for metrics datasets.

204.description: Map field removed. No response body.

400.description: The dataset is a metrics dataset.

404.description: The dataset doesn't exist or the field isn't a map field.

get.description: Lists monitors in the organization, sorted by name. Only returns monitors that query at least one dataset visible to the caller. Labels are resolved unless `exclude=labels`.

parameters.description: Exclude resolved label objects from each monitor response. The labelIds field is still returned.
parameters.name: exclude

parameters.description: Return monitors assigned every specified label ID.
parameters.name: labelIds

post.description: Creates a monitor. Axiom runs the monitor's query once before saving it and rejects the request if the query fails, for example because it's invalid or references a dataset that doesn't exist.

get.description: Retrieves a monitor by ID. Returns `404` if the monitor doesn't exist or the caller can't query its datasets. Labels are resolved unless `exclude=labels`.

parameters.description: Monitor ID.
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: Exclude resolved label objects from the monitor response. The labelIds field is still returned.
parameters.name: exclude

put.description: Replaces a monitor's configuration with the request body, so omitted fields reset to their defaults. Axiom runs the new query once before saving, and the update clears the monitor's current alert state.

parameters.description: Monitor ID.
parameters.name: id

delete.description: Permanently deletes a monitor and removes its label assignments. The caller needs query access to the monitor's datasets.

parameters.description: Monitor ID.
parameters.name: id

get.description: Lists the notifications sent for the monitor between `startTime` and `endTime`. Each delivery is a separate item: one per notifier, and one per recipient for email notifiers. Failed deliveries are included. State changes that sent no notification, for example while the monitor had no notifiers, aren't listed. The caller needs query access to the monitor's datasets.

parameters.description: Monitor ID.
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: Start of the time range (RFC 3339).
parameters.name: startTime

parameters.description: End of the time range (RFC 3339). Must not be before `startTime`.
parameters.name: endTime

200.description: Notifications sent in the time range.

get.description: Lists all notifiers in the organization, sorted by name. Labels are resolved unless `exclude=labels`.

parameters.description: Exclude resolved label objects from each notifier response. The labelIds field is still returned.
parameters.name: exclude

post.description: Creates a notifier. Set exactly one channel under `properties`, such as `slack`, `email`, or `webhook`. Returns `400` if the channel type isn't enabled for your organization.

get.description: Retrieves a notifier by ID. Labels are resolved unless `exclude=labels`.

parameters.description: Notifier ID.
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: Exclude resolved label objects from the notifier response. The labelIds field is still returned.
parameters.name: exclude

put.description: Replaces a notifier's name, channel `properties`, and `disabledUntil` with the request body, so omitted fields are cleared. Label assignments are unchanged.

parameters.description: Notifier ID.
parameters.name: id

delete.description: Permanently deletes a notifier and removes its label assignments. Returns `400` if any monitor still uses the notifier.

parameters.description: Notifier ID.
parameters.name: id

get.description: Lists the organizations the authenticated user is a member of. Requires a personal access token (PAT). Organizations that enforce SAML sign-in are omitted unless the PAT is SAML-authenticated.

200.description: Organizations the user is a member of.

post.description: Creates an organization on the Personal plan with the authenticated user as its owner. Requires a personal access token (PAT).

400.description: Invalid name or edge deployment, or the user has reached the maximum number of organizations.

get.description: Retrieves an organization the authenticated user is a member of, including its plan and license limits. Requires a personal access token (PAT).

404.description: Organization not found, or the user isn't a member of it.

put.description: Renames an organization and returns the updated organization. Requires a personal access token (PAT) of an owner of the organization.

400.description: Invalid name.

403.description: The user isn't an owner of the organization.

post.description: Creates a temporary organization for an automated agent and returns a full-permission API token and a claim URL. The organization is deleted after 24 hours unless a human claims it. Doesn't require authentication and is rate limited per client IP.
post.summary: Provision a temporary organization for an agent

400.description: Invalid name or edge deployment.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded, either for the client IP or for all callers. Retry later with backoff.

get.description: Lists the custom roles in the organization with their capabilities and the IDs of users assigned each role directly. Built-in roles such as `axiom-admin` aren't included.

post.description: Creates a custom role. Requires an Enterprise plan or the RBAC add-on. The name must be unique and can't start with `axiom-`. The `members` field is ignored; assign users with the Update user role endpoint.

requestBody.description: The role's name, description, and capabilities

get.description: Retrieves a custom role by ID with its capabilities and the IDs of users assigned the role directly. Built-in role IDs such as `axiom-admin` return `404`.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the role to retrieve
parameters.name: id

put.description: Replaces a custom role's name, description, and capabilities. Capabilities you omit are removed, and the `members` field is ignored. Requires an Enterprise plan or the RBAC add-on.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the role to update
parameters.name: id

requestBody.description: The role's new name, description, and capabilities

delete.description: Permanently deletes a custom role. Users assigned the role get the `none` role, and the role is removed from all groups. Requires an Enterprise plan or the RBAC add-on.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the role to delete
parameters.name: id

get.description: Lists all groups in the organization with the role IDs and user IDs assigned to each group.

post.description: Creates a group whose members get the group's roles. Requires an Enterprise plan or the RBAC add-on. The name must be unique, every role ID must exist, and you can't add yourself as a member.

requestBody.description: The group's name, description, roles, and members

get.description: Retrieves a group by ID with its role IDs, member user IDs, and whether it's managed by your identity provider (`isManaged`).

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the group to retrieve
parameters.name: id

put.description: Replaces a group's name, description, roles, and members. Fields you omit are cleared, and members of managed groups aren't changed. Requires an Enterprise plan or the RBAC add-on.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the group to update
parameters.name: id

requestBody.description: The group's new name, description, roles, and members

delete.description: Permanently deletes a group. Members lose the roles the group granted but keep their own role, and dashboards the group owned are shared with everyone. Managed groups can't be deleted. Requires an Enterprise plan or the RBAC add-on.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the group to delete
parameters.name: id

get.description: Lists saved APL queries on datasets you can read, sorted by name. Use `who` to choose whose queries to return, and `limit` and `offset` to paginate.

parameters.description: Return only queries saved on this dataset.
parameters.name: dataset

parameters.description:
- If the value of `who` is your own user ID, the request returns queries saved by the authenticated user.
- If the value of `who` is `team`, the request returns queries saved by other users in the organization. For example, `&who=team`.
- If the value of `who` is `all`, the request returns queries saved by all users in the organization, including the authenticated user. For example, `&who=all`.
- Any other value returns `400`. This includes another user's ID, and omitting `who` when you authenticate with a personal access token.
parameters.name: who

parameters.description: Return only queries whose name contains this string. Case-insensitive.
parameters.name: qs

400.description: Invalid `who`.

404.description: You can't read the dataset in `dataset`.

post.description: Saves an APL query for the authenticated user. Axiom sets `who` to the caller and `kind` to `apl`. If you omit `dataset`, Axiom uses the alphabetically first dataset that `query.apl` references.

400.description: Missing `name`, or no `dataset` given and none found in `query.apl`.

403.description: You don't have permission to create saved queries on the dataset.

get.description: Retrieves a saved query by its ID.

404.description: Saved query not found, or you can't read its dataset.

put.description: Replaces the `name`, `dataset`, `query`, and `metadata` of a saved query. With a personal access token, you can only update queries you saved.

400.description: Missing `name`, or no `dataset` given and none found in `query.apl`.

401.description: The saved query belongs to another user.

403.description: You don't have permission to update saved queries on the current or new dataset.

delete.description: Deletes a saved query by its ID. With a personal access token, you can only delete queries you saved.

401.description: The saved query belongs to another user.

403.description: You don't have permission to delete saved queries on the query's dataset.

get.description: Lists the organization's active API tokens. Expired tokens, personal access tokens, and token secret values aren't included.

post.description: Creates an API token and returns its secret `token` value, which you can't retrieve again. You can only grant capabilities you have yourself. If you omit `expiresAt`, the token doesn't expire.

200.description: Created API token, including its secret `token` value.

400.description: No capability set, an invalid capability, or a capability the caller doesn't have.

get.description: Retrieves an active API token by ID. The response doesn't include the token's secret value.

404.description: API token not found or expired.

delete.description: Permanently deletes an API token so it can no longer authenticate requests.

404.description: API token not found or expired.

post.description: Creates a new API token with the existing token's capabilities, or with those in `newToken`, and returns its secret value. The existing token keeps working until `existingTokenExpiresAt`; set it to the current time to revoke it immediately.

200.description: New API token, including its secret `token` value.

400.description: Missing `existingTokenExpiresAt`, expiry set in both `newTokenExpiresAt` and `newToken.expiresAt`, or invalid capabilities in `newToken`.

404.description: API token not found or expired.

get.description: Retrieves the user who owns the personal access token (PAT) used to authenticate. API tokens aren't supported. The response includes `role` only when the `X-AXIOM-ORG-ID` header is set.

403.description: The request was authenticated with an API token, or the user isn't a member of the organization in `X-AXIOM-ORG-ID`.

put.description: Updates the name of the user who owns the personal access token (PAT) used to authenticate. API tokens aren't supported. The response doesn't include `role`.

400.description: Invalid name, or the request was authenticated with an API token.

get.description: Lists all members of the organization, including each member's role.

post.description: Adds a user to the organization with the given role and sends them an invite email. If the email address already belongs to an Axiom account, Axiom keeps its existing name. API tokens can't assign the `owner` role.

400.description: Invalid email address, the user is already a member, or the organization has reached its user limit.

403.description: Insufficient permissions, or the caller isn't allowed to assign the `owner` role.

get.description: Retrieves a member of the organization by user ID, including their role.

delete.description: Removes a user from the organization without deleting their Axiom account. You can't remove the organization's last member. With a personal access token (PAT), only owners can remove an owner.

put.description: Changes the role of a member of the organization and returns the updated user. You can't change your own role. Only owners using a personal access token (PAT) can assign `owner` or change an owner's role.

403.description: Insufficient permissions, you tried to change your own role, or the caller isn't allowed to assign or change the `owner` role.

get.description: Lists the virtual fields of a dataset, ordered by creation time.

parameters.description: Name of the dataset
parameters.name: dataset

post.description: Creates a virtual field on a dataset. Axiom sets its ID to `<dataset>.<name>`, so the name must be unique within the dataset. `expression` must be a valid APL expression.

400.description: Missing `dataset`, `name`, or `expression`, an invalid `name`, or an expression that doesn't parse.

403.description: You don't have permission to create virtual fields on the dataset.

409.description: A virtual field with this name already exists on the dataset.

get.description: Retrieves a virtual field by its ID.

parameters.description: ID of the virtual field in the form `<dataset>.<name>`
parameters.name: id

404.description: Virtual field not found, or you can't read its dataset.

put.description: Replaces all fields of a virtual field. Omitted optional fields are cleared. The ID doesn't change, even if you change `name` or `dataset`.

parameters.description: ID of the virtual field in the form `<dataset>.<name>`
parameters.name: id

400.description: Missing `dataset`, `name`, or `expression`, an invalid `name`, or an expression that doesn't parse.

403.description: You don't have permission to update virtual fields on the current or new dataset.

delete.description: Deletes a virtual field by its ID.

parameters.description: ID of the virtual field in the form `<dataset>.<name>`
parameters.name: id

403.description: You don't have permission to delete virtual fields on the dataset.

404.description: Virtual field not found, or you can't read its dataset.

get.description: Lists the views in the organization, including views shared with it by other organizations.

post.description: Creates a view, a named APL query that you can query like a dataset. Axiom derives `datasets` from `aplQuery`. The name can't match an existing dataset or view, and the query can't reference views or use wildcards.

400.description: Invalid view, for example an APL parse error, a name that's already in use, or a query that references a view or datasets in different regions.

403.description: You don't have query access to a dataset that `aplQuery` references.

get.description: Retrieves a view by its name.

parameters.description: Name of the view
parameters.name: id

403.description: You don't have query access to the view's dataset.

put.description: Replaces the `aplQuery` and `description` of a view, identified by its name. Axiom ignores `name` and `datasets` in the body and derives `datasets` from the new query.

parameters.description: Name of the view
parameters.name: id

403.description: You don't have query access to the view's current or new datasets.

delete.description: Deletes a view by its name.

parameters.description: Name of the view
parameters.name: id

403.description: You don't have query access to the view's dataset.

get.description: Lists dashboards visible to the caller, sorted by name and paginated with `limit` and `offset`. Labels are resolved unless `exclude=labels`.

parameters.name: exclude
parameters.description: Exclude resolved label objects from each dashboard response. The labelIds field is still returned.

parameters.name: labelIds
parameters.description: Return dashboards assigned every specified label ID.

400.description: Invalid label filter

post.description: Creates a dashboard and generates a `uid` if you don't set one. If a dashboard with the `uid` already exists, updates it and returns `200`, which requires the current `version` or `overwrite: true`.

400.description: Invalid dashboard payload

get.description: Retrieves a dashboard by UID, including its current `version`. Labels are resolved unless `exclude=labels`.

parameters.name: exclude
parameters.description: Exclude resolved label objects from the dashboard response. The labelIds field is still returned.

put.description: Replaces the dashboard document for the UID. Set `version` to the current version, or `overwrite: true` to skip the check; a stale `version` returns `412`. Creates the dashboard and returns `201` if the UID doesn't exist.

400.description: Invalid dashboard payload

delete.description: Permanently deletes a dashboard by UID and removes its label assignments. Returns `404` if the dashboard doesn't exist or the caller can't manage it.

patch.description: Applies a JSON merge patch to one chart in a dashboard. Set `version` to the dashboard's current version, or `overwrite: true` to skip the check; a stale `version` returns `412`.

400.description: Invalid dashboard chart patch

Auth.description: Authenticate using an API token or personal access token (PAT). Include the token as a Bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. For more information, see [Tokens](/reference/tokens).

bearerAuth.description: Authenticate using an API token or personal access token (PAT). Include the token as a Bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. For more information, see [Tokens](/reference/tokens).

apiLastUsed.description: When the token was last used on an API other than ingest

expiresAt.description: Expiration date of the token (ISO 8601 format)

ingestLastUsed.description: When the token was last used to ingest

AggInfo.description: AggInfo captures information about an aggregation

args.description: Args specifies any non-field arguments for the aggregation. Fx. [10] for topk(players, 10).

fields.description:
Fields specifies the names of the fields this aggregation is computed on.
Fx ["players"] for topk(players, 10)

name.description:
Name is the system name of the aggregation, which is the string form of aggregation.Type.
If the aggregation is aliased, the alias is stored in the parent FieldInfo

AlertHistory.description: A notification sent for a monitor.

name.description: Title of the notification: `Triggered: ` or `Resolved: ` followed by the monitor name

state.description: `open` if the notification reported that the monitor triggered, `closed` if it reported that the monitor resolved

timestamp.description: Time the delivery was recorded, after any retries

datasets.description: array<string> of dataset names for which the annotation appears on charts

description.description: Explanation of the event the annotation marks on the charts

time.description: Time the annotation marks on the charts. If you don't include this field, Axiom assigns the time of the API request to the annotation.

title.description: Summary of the annotation that appears on the charts

type.description: Type of the event marked by the annotation. Use only alphanumeric characters or hyphens. For example, "production-deployment".

url.description: URL relevant for the event marked by the annotation. For example, link to GitHub pull request.

example.description: Deploy new feature to the sales form
example.title: Production deployment

Modules.description: Key-value pairs of module names and module sources. Axiom will make modules available for this query later.

startTime.description:
start and end time for the query, these must be specified as RFC3339 strings
or using relative time expressions (e.g. now-1h, now-1d, now-1w, etc)

variables.description: Variables is an optional set of additional variables that are inserted into the APL

description.description: The description of the apl module definition.

id.description: The unique identifier for the object.

name.description: The name of the apl module definition.

namespace.description: The namespace of the APL module definition.

code.description: Status is the http status code associated with this error

column.description: Column is the column associated with this compile type error

compileErrorCode.description:
CompileErrorCode is a special error code that is only available for Compile Errors
It is an integer value that can be used to identify the error

errorType.description: Error Type is an integer value indicating the kind of error

line.description: Line is the line associated with this compile type error

message.description: Message is the raw error message without any formatting

tables.description: Tables hold the result data for a query

BucketInfo.description: The standard mode of operation for Kirby is to create buckets on the _time column,
BucketInfo.title: BucketInfo captures information about how a grouped query is sorted into buckets.

field.description: Field specifies the field used to create buckets on. Normally this would be _time.

size.description:
An integer or float representing the fixed bucket size.
When the bucket field is _time this value is in nanoseconds.

collections.description: Map of collection name to the RFC3339 time of its last change.

expiresAt.description: Expiration date of the token (ISO 8601 format)

retentionDays.description: Number of days to retain data in the dataset

useRetentionPeriod.description: Ignored. Axiom derives this value from `retentionDays`.

CreateUserRequest.description: Object representing a new user creation request

email.description: Email address of the new user

name.description: Full name of the new user

role.description: Role to assign to the new user

CustomNotifierConfig.description:
Configuration for custom webhook notifications with flexible headers and body template.
Supports variable substitution in the body template using {{.Variable}} syntax.

body.description: Template for the webhook body, supports variable substitution

headers.description: HTTP headers to include in the request

secretHeaders.description: Sensitive HTTP headers (tokens, keys) that should be masked in logs

chart.description: JSON merge patch applied to the existing chart. If id is present, it must match the chartId path parameter.

version.description: Required for updates when overwrite is false.

DashboardVariable.description: A variable defines an APL variable that is available to a dashboard

default.description: If set, should be the default value for this variable in the dashboard

kind.description: A kind allows for different kinds of variables to be treated differently depending on what they are used for. A refless kind indicates that it's just a plain variable and we can not derive possible values from it A datadog kind indicates that we will use the ref value as a lookup against a datadog tag

ref.description: The ref value indicates where this variable can derive its values from

values.description: Values is an indication of possible values for this variable, it may not be all the possible values just known quantities

canWrite.description: Whether this dataset has write access

created.description: The RFC3339-formatted time when the dataset was created.

labelIds.description: IDs of labels assigned to this dataset.

labels.description: Resolved labels assigned to this dataset.

retentionDays.description: Number of days to retain data in the dataset

sharedByOrg.description: ID of the org that shared this resource, if it's shared

updatedAt.description: The RFC3339-formatted time when the dataset was last updated.

useRetentionPeriod.description: Whether to use the retention period

active30d.description: Fields with a non-null value in the last 30 days. Omitted if presence stats fail.

fieldCount.description: Number of fields in the dataset catalog.

fieldLimit.description: Organization field limit. Null when the org has no field cap.

growth.description: Fields first registered in each window. Fields with no firstSeen are skipped.

30d.description: Fields first registered in the last 30 days.

7d.description: Fields first registered in the last 7 days.

headroom.description: fieldLimit minus fieldCount. Can be negative. Null when fieldLimit is null.

inactive30d.description: Fields with no non-null value in the last 30 days. Omitted if presence stats fail.

topGrowthSources.description: Parent paths with the most fields first registered in the last 7 days.

newFields7d.description: Fields first registered under this prefix in the last 7 days.

prefix.description: Parent dotted path of the new fields.

fieldCount.description: Number of fields in the dataset catalog.

unused.description: Catalog fields with a name or type absent from blocks.

example.message: Vacuuming a metrics dataset is not supported

DiscordConfig.description: Configuration for Discord notifications using bot token

discordChannel.description: Discord channel ID to send notifications

DiscordWebhookConfig.description: Configuration for Discord notifications using webhooks

environmentDefault.description: Whether the edge deployment is the default for the environment

emails.description: List of email addresses to receive notifications

FieldInfo.title: FieldInfo captures information about a field used in the tabular result format. See Table.

Group.description: Defines a group of users for organizational purposes

description.description: Detailed description of the group's purpose and scope

isManaged.description: Whether the group is synced from your identity provider. You can't delete a managed group or change its members.

members.description: List of user IDs that are assigned to this group

name.description: Unique name identifier for the group

roles.description: IDs of the roles assigned to the group. Use a custom role ID or a built-in role ID: `axiom-owner`, `axiom-admin`, `axiom-user`, `axiom-read-only`, or `axiom-none`.

GroupInfo.title: GroupInfo captures information about a grouping clause in the tabular result format. See Table.

GroupWithID.description: Extends the base Group type to include a unique identifier

token.description: The raw token value to identify

createdAt.description: When the token was created (ISO 8601 format)

createdBy.description: User ID or token ID of the creator

LabelAssignmentTarget.description: A resource that supports organization labels. The target type determines which identifier is required.

dataset.description: Required for dataset targets, which reject id, uid, and templateId. Also required alongside templateId for frontend integration dashboards. Use the current dataset name. Assignments use the underlying dataset instance, so permanent deletion and recreation do not restore old labels.

id.description: Required for monitor and notifier targets, using the ID returned by their respective APIs. Also identifies a backend-provided integration dashboard using the opaque ID returned by backend dashboard listing APIs. Mutually exclusive with uid, templateId, and dataset.

templateId.description: Stable frontend-owned template key for an integration_dashboard target, such as k8s.stats. Requires dataset and rejects id and uid. The backend treats this key as opaque and does not validate a template registry. Whitespace and control characters are rejected.

uid.description: Required only for saved dashboard targets; rejected for other target types.

Monitor.description:
Configuration for a monitoring rule. Monitors can be configured to:
- Check threshold values (e.g., CPU usage > 90%)
- Match specific events in logs
- Detect anomalies based on historical patterns
Each monitor runs on a specified interval and can trigger notifications through configured notifiers.

alertOnNoData.description: Whether to alert when no data is received

aplQuery.description:
APL (Axiom Processing Language) query string used for monitoring.
This query defines what data to analyze and how to process it.
At least one of aplQuery or mplQuery must be provided.

columnName.description: Name of the column to monitor

compareDays.description: Number of days to compare for anomaly detection

description.description: Detailed description of the monitor's purpose
description.example: Monitors CPU usage and alerts when it exceeds 90%

disabled.description: Whether the monitor is currently disabled

disabledUntil.description: Timestamp until when the monitor should remain disabled

intervalMinutes.description:
How frequently the monitor should run, in minutes.
Minimum value is 1 minute.

mplQuery.description:
MPL (Metrics Processing Language) query string for metrics-based monitoring.
Use this as an alternative to aplQuery for metrics datasets.
At least one of aplQuery or mplQuery must be provided.

notifierIds.description:
List of notifier IDs that will receive alerts.
Notifiers can be email, Slack, webhook endpoints, etc.

notifyEveryRun.description: Whether to send notifications on every check

operator.description:
Comparison operator for threshold checks:
- Below: Trigger when value < threshold
- BelowOrEqual: Trigger when value <= threshold
- Above: Trigger when value > threshold
- AboveOrEqual: Trigger when value >= threshold
- AboveOrBelow: Trigger when value is outside a range

rangeMinutes.description:
Time window to evaluate in each check, in minutes.
For example, "last 5 minutes of data"

resolvable.description: Whether the alert can be manually resolved

secondDelay.description: Delay in seconds before triggering the alert

threshold.description: Threshold value for triggering the alert

triggerAfterNPositiveResults.description: Number of positive results needed before triggering

triggerFromNRuns.description:
Number of consecutive check runs that must fail before triggering an alert.
Use this to avoid alerting on temporary spikes.

type.description:
Type of monitoring check to perform:
- Threshold: Compares a numeric value against a threshold
- MatchEvent: Looks for specific events or patterns
- AnomalyDetection: Identifies unusual patterns based on historical data

against.description: Relative time comparison offset. Compares the current time window against a previous period offset by this duration. Mutually exclusive with `againstTimestamp` — setting one clears the other. Use an empty string or omit to disable comparison.

againstTimestamp.description: Absolute or relative timestamp to compare against. Mutually exclusive with `against` — setting one clears the other. Accepts ISO 8601, `now-{duration}` (e.g. `now-1h`), or epoch milliseconds as a string.

Owner.description: User ID of the dashboard owner. Use `X-AXIOM-EVERYONE` to make the dashboard accessible to all users in the organization.

DatetimeString.description: A datetime value. Accepts ISO 8601 (e.g. `2024-01-02T00:00:00.000Z`), relative time using `now-{duration}` where duration is a number followed by `s` (seconds), `m` (minutes), `h` (hours), `d` (days), or `w` (weeks) (e.g. `now-1h`, `now-7d`), a Unix epoch millisecond timestamp as a string (e.g. `1704067200000`), or an empty string to clear the value.

displayNull.description: Controls how empty intervals are rendered in time series charts. `auto` infers from the query, `null` leaves gaps, `span` connects adjacent points, `zero` fills with zero.

overlayCharts.description: When enabled, charts are overlaid on a single chart instead of stacked separately.

options.description: Pre-defined options merged with the dynamic options returned by `query` at runtime. Typically used to seed a default option (for example an "All" entry with `unset: true`) so the filter has a sensible initial selection before — or independent of — query results.

apl.description:
APL query that returns the list of options for the filter dropdown. The result must contain a `key` column and a `value` column — Axiom interprets each row as a `{ key, value }` pair for an option. Use `distinct` to collapse the source field to unique values, then `project` to expose the `key` and `value` columns.

Example:
```
['dataset-name'] | distinct field_name | project key=field_name, value=field_name
```

mpl.description:
MPL query that returns the list of options for the filter dropdown. The query must group by exactly one tag — Axiom uses each distinct value of that tag as both the key and the value of an option. Use `align using last` to simplify the query.

Example:
```
dataset:metric | align using last | group by tag using count
```

TimeWindowStart.description: Start of the dashboard time range. Use `qr-now-{duration}` for a quick range relative to now, where duration is a number followed by `s` (seconds), `m` (minutes), `h` (hours), `d` (days), or `w` (weeks). Examples: `qr-now-5m`, `qr-now-1h`, `qr-now-7d`. Alternatively, use a Unix epoch millisecond timestamp as a string (e.g. `1704067200000`).

TimeWindowEnd.description: End of the dashboard time range. Use `qr-now` for a rolling window that tracks the current time (pair with a `qr-now-{duration}` start), or a Unix epoch millisecond timestamp as a string (e.g. `1704153600000`).

DashboardUID.description: Optional dashboard UID. Must contain only letters, numbers, underscores, or hyphens, with length 1-128 when provided.
